winner.title: Ema Datshi

evidence.authenticity: Traditional method (chillies simmered with onion, garlic, tomato in water, heat off, then butter and cheese). Article stresses chillies are the main ingredient, warns against fondue-style versions, notes dish eaten in Bhutan/Kalimpong, serves with rice or tingmo.
evidence.precision: Metric weights for all 10 ingredients (220 g jalapenos, 15 g garlic, 75 g cheese, 250 g water). Doneness cue: ~15 min medium until peppers softened; taste and adjust salt by cheese. No pan size. Cues on only 1 or 2 steps.
evidence.testing: Reasoning given: mixed chillies for flavour vs heat, heat off before cheese to prevent curdling, avoid stringy cheeses, cheese saltiness varies. Rating 97.3 over 5188 votes.
evidence.photos: No step-by-step photos; only finished-dish and in-Bhutan photos.
evidence.efficiency: 25 min total, single pot, nothing wasted.
evidence.access: Real datshi is unobtainable in the US. Page says use any good melting cheese, processed cheese in a pinch, avoid mozzarella. Jalapenos are easy to find.

winner.why: Only candidate with full gram weights, a clear doneness cue and explained reasoning, and it is the most faithful to the traditional chilli-forward dish.

runnerUp.title: Bhutanese Ema Datshi Recipe

evidence.authenticity: Same method as Bong Eats (appears adapted from it), with volume measures.
evidence.precision: Mostly cup/tsp volumes, one weight (8 oz jalapenos); softened-peppers cue.

runnerUp.why: Same technique but with vaguer volume measures and no explanation.
